body:
# Numerical stationary-section chart audit

This note corrects a numerical issue. It proves no geometric inequality.

The numerical routines in `supporting computation general-stationary-section-screen.py` and
`supporting computation general-scalar-centroid-correction-screen.py` solve for a central plane
normal in one of three coordinate charts. They initially fixed one raw
normal coordinate to1 and asked that the other two coordinates of the
section centroid vanish. Algebraically, at a finite chart point this
implies the third coordinate vanishes, because the centroid lies in the
plane. Numerically, however, the two free normal coordinates can diverge.
After normalization the fixed normal coordinate tends to0, so the third
centroid coordinate is not controlled by the two residuals. A numerical
root in this limit is not a certified stationary section.

An apparent scalar-centroid-correction obstruction had normalized normal
approximately(-.997555,.069889,0) and section centroid approximately
(0,0,.623176). It is invalid. Its raw output is retained under the explicit
name `supporting computation invalid-scalar-correction-chart-pole-candidate.json`.

Both routines now reject a candidate unless the Euclidean norm of the
FULL three-dimensional section centroid is at most1e-7. This is still
numerical screening, not an exact proof or a rigorous existence certificate.

Consequently the old 50-body screen's list of stationary directions must
not be cited as verified geometric data. The absence of violations in
that larger, partly spurious list is at most computational screening
history. Any future claimed counterexample must independently certify
all three section-centroid coordinates and the exact inequalities.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
